We're in this web of fast technology (fast transportation, fast information networks, fast images), which disconnects us from our natural rhythms (walking, sleep cycles, seasons).

Your perception of speed is directly tied to how much variety you have in your life. If you do the same thing every day then time will speed by for you. This is of course what most of us will experience with a full time job. You can mitigate it a little by going out and doing something different every weekend. Of course playing the same game or working on the same hobby again and again over the weekend will not help.

The "faster" thing is just a lifestyle choice. It's certainly not Necessary to live, and live well. Personally, I don't have a for-pay job (and my wife works 3 days a week), we live in VERY rural Georgia where it's exceeding cheap to live. For example, my historic/1930's brick tudor house cost us just $60k to purchase (under $500/month for loan, taxes, insurance). I don't own a watch because I don't have to worry about time. Similarly, my cell phone is an old 'dumb' phone from ~2008.

Those who don't want "fast", can easily avoid it. It's just that most people Want the trappings of "fast" in some respects and thus MUST have fast in others (unavoidable). There are concessions that have to be made... for instance, there's no place within an hours drive of me where I willing would go to eat. As it happens, I already enjoy cooking so it's no big deal, but I know a lot of people think going out to eat is a happy treat (or maybe even a necessity). Similarly, going to the grocery store is a 3+ hour outing (roughly an hour drive each way and an hour in the store).

Guess what I do on those long drives? I certainly don't play with a phone (whatever people do with smartphones, talk with my phone that's only a phone). I don't speed either, because there's simply no hurry. I think, contemplate, relax. I do it every ~10 days or so. At home (doing a lot of restoration work), I'm most frequently found with earplugs in and doing work... slow, tedious, meditating type work. Or I'm in the garden weeding/tending, or I'm walking my dog. There's really NO rush to anything in my life unless I want it there.

So, even if society is in a rush, it's all individual choices. No one is being MADE to live fast, each person chooses. Don't like it? Change. There are a million different variations to fit any/all preferences. I certainly haven't lived this way my whole life (though starting out by being born/raised in very rural Wyoming doesn't hurt), it's just where I prefer to be now and likely through the rest of my life.
